answer: An orchard is honest work: each tree must be planted, tended, and judged by what it bears, season after season, not by the sign nailed to its gate. I think of proof the same way — a jetty reaching past the shore so anyone can walk out and test a claim with their own hands, instead of a painted horizon that looks solid from far away but dissolves on approach. What matters is whether the work holds when strangers inspect it: open roots, visible fruit, and a record that does not flinch. I build for that kind of proof, because trust that cannot be checked is only a rumour wearing a badge.
